subject: PO consolidation + marketplace renewal sync (Medivance)
messages:
From: Sara Lopez <sara@medivance.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medivance.com
Date: 2028-05-05T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Marketplace renewal sync + single PO request

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. We reviewed our renewals and across AWS, Azure and GCP the current commitments are staggered (see attached renewal_matrix.xlsx). Procurement is pushing to simplify: we want a single purchase order and invoicing cadence for the upcoming 12–24 month renewals instead of three separate POs across marketplaces.

Key constraints on our side:
- Need private-offer / marketplace paperwork to be aligned so our legal team can sign one PO and have it applied to each marketplace acceptance window.
- Azure acceptance window is tight (end of May) — we need DocuSign-ready documents this week or we risk missing the tranche.
- Tax/VAT info + billing contact must be clear on each PO.

Can Redwood accommodate a consolidated PO approach that maps to three private-offer numbers (one per cloud) and a single invoice cadence? If so, please send a short mutual action plan and a PO template we can hand to procurement.

I attached a renewal matrix for transparency. We can do a call tomorrow afternoon if that helps.

Best,
Sara Lopez
Head of Procurement
Medivance

Attachment: renewal_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lopez <sara@medivance.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-05T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace renewal sync + single PO request

Sara — thanks for the clear summary and the matrix. We can support the consolidated-PO pattern but there are a few operational caveats to keep in mind:

1) Marketplace mechanics: each cloud (AWS / Azure / GCP) still requires its own private-offer ID and acceptance flow. We can attach a single customer PO to each private-offer acceptance, and route invoices on a single cadence, but acceptance dates must satisfy each marketplace's evidence window.

2) Azure window: we can target DocuSign today/tomorrow. Kimberly will handle the Azure private-offer packaging and confirm the acceptance ID.

3) Tax & billing: please confirm billing entity (legal name + tax id) and preferred invoice cadence (monthly / quarterly / annual). Our finance team needs that to populate the PO.

Action items (proposed):
- Redwood: produce a 1-page mutual action plan + three private-offer IDs mapped to the single PO (Ben).
- Procurement: confirm billing entity and signatory (Sara).
- Legal: we’ll prepare Master PO template and DocuSign envelope (Kimberly).

I’ve attached a draft PO template (medivance_po_draft.pdf) — please review and flag any procurement-specific language you need. I’ll send a brief MAP (mutual action plan) in a reply from Ben so we have timelines.

Thanks — we’ll treat Azure as highest priority for timing.

— Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: medivance_po_draft.pdf (PDF stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lopez <sara@medivance.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-06T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace renewal sync + single PO request

Sara / team — attaching a short MAP and a proposed sequencing (see MAP_medivance_v2.docx). High-level approach that should address procurement constraints:

- Step 1 (today): Redwood prepares three private-offer drafts (AWS / Azure / GCP) that reference a single customer PO number and the same invoice cadence. Each private-offer will have its own acceptance ID but include a clause linking them to the master PO.
- Step 2 (Azure priority): Kimberly will upload the Azure package by EOD Monday to capture the acceptance window.
- Step 3 (Billing): Redwood Finance (cc’d) will accept a single legal entity for invoicing; invoices will be generated per the agreed cadence and include marketplace-specific line items for visibility.
- Step 4 (DocuSign): We’ll send a DocuSign envelope containing the master PO and the Azure offer first, then AWS/GCP offers as counters to be accepted within 10 business days.

Risks & mitigations:
- If Azure acceptance misses the window, we can still process an off-cycle acceptance but terms may shift; we’ll flag that in the MAP.
- Multi-cloud tax handling: Priyom will confirm VAT/tax fields that need to be present in each private-offer.

Action owners & ETA:
- Ben: share MAP and private-offer drafts (today).
- Kimberly: Azure package upload (EOD Monday).
- Priyom: tax field confirmation (tomorrow).
- Sara: confirm billing entity + signer (asap).

Let me know if you prefer a 30-minute sync; otherwise we’ll proceed by email and get the DocuSign envelope out.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: MAP_medivance_v2.docx (Word doc stub)

From: Sara Lopez <sara@medivance.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medivance.com
Date: 2028-05-07T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace renewal sync + single PO request

Thanks Ben — that plan looks good. A couple quick confirmations from procurement:

- Billing entity: Medivance, Inc. (TIN: 12-3456789). Please place billing contact as: Finance Ops <finance-ops@medivance.com>.
- Invoice cadence: quarterly invoices preferred.
- Azure is highest priority — please get the DocuSign envelope for the Azure offer + master PO by EOD tomorrow.
- We are fine with private-offer IDs per cloud as long as the master PO number maps to each acceptance record.

We’re available for a 20-minute call tomorrow 11:00–12:00 PT if you want to run through the MAP live. Otherwise please proceed with the DocuSign.

Sara Lopez
Head of Procurement
Medivance
